title: Cookbook:Carrots Cooked Kinpira Style
ingredients_raw: 1 Tbsp vegetable oil, preferably sesame oil
Tamari or shoyu soy sauce, to taste
steps: Cut the carrots into thin matchstick pieces (sen-giri, or julienned)
Pour a small amount of oil into a saucepan and sauté the carrot pieces briefly
Add just enough water to half-cover the carrot pieces
Place the lid on the pot and let the carrots simmer briefly on medium-low heat
Add a little tamari or shoyu to enhance flavour. Serve.
description: Kinpira is a Japanese cooking term that roughly translates to sauté and simmer. The aim is to cook root vegetables such as carrots and burdock root in a minimum amount of water so that they end up tenderly cooked and with none of their flavour or nutritional value lost into discarded cooking water.

'''Kinpira''' is a [[Cookbook:Cuisine of Japan|Japanese]] cooking term that roughly translates to ''[[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] and [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]]''. The aim is to cook root vegetables such as carrots and burdock root in a minimum amount of water so that they end up tenderly cooked and with none of their flavour or nutritional value lost into discarded cooking water.

==Ingredients==
*250 g (½ lb) [[Cookbook:Carrot|carrot]]s, [[Cookbook:Julienne|julienned]]
*1 Tbsp [[cookbook:Vegetable oil|vegetable oil]], preferably [[Cookbook:Sesame Oil|sesame oil]]
*[[Cookbook:Water|Water]]
*Tamari or shoyu [[Cookbook:Soy Sauce|soy sauce]], to taste

==Procedure==
# Cut the carrots into thin matchstick pieces (sen-giri, or [[Cookbook:Julienne|julienned]])
# Pour a small amount of oil into a [[cookbook:saucepan|saucepan]] and [[Cookbook:Sautéing|sauté]] the carrot pieces briefly
# Add just enough water to half-cover the carrot pieces
# Place the lid on the pot and let the carrots [[Cookbook:Simmering|simmer]] briefly on medium-low heat
# Add a little tamari or shoyu to enhance flavour. Serve.
